title: Popcorn stitch
subtitle: Five complete trebles, lifted and closed into a tight round bump
excerpt: The popcorn makes five complete trebles in the same stitch, removes the hook from the loop, inserts it into the first treble of the group, and pulls through — lifting the whole cluster into a tall, defined bump. Firmer than a bobble, with a flat back that sits cleanly against the fabric.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volume 4 (Internet Archive). Textured crochet stitches including popcorn constructions. Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886).
heroPrompt: A close-up swatch of popcorn stitch showing the tall, round, defined bumps standing proud of the fabric surface in cream DK cotton, soft daylight, plain background.

glossaryTerms.definition: Five complete trebles worked into the same base stitch. The hook is removed from the working loop, re-inserted into the top of the first treble, and the working loop is pulled through to close — lifting the whole cluster into a tall, firm bump.

content.text: is firmer and taller than a bobble. Where a bobble stacks incomplete trebles, a popcorn completes each treble fully before closing the group. The result stands higher above the surface, with a round defined top and a flat back — which is why it is the stitch of choice for Aran-style afghan squares.
Work 5 complete trebles into the same stitch. Each treble is finished normally (yarn over and pull through the last two loops).
Remove the hook from the working loop carefully — hold the loop with a finger or let it relax on a safety pin if you are working a loose yarn.
Insert the hook from front to back through the top of the FIRST treble of the five-treble group (the V at the very top of the first treble).
Pick up the working loop and pull it through the first treble top. One loop on hook. The cluster is lifted and the top is now closed.
Optional ch 1 to anchor the popcorn. Work into the next stitch as normal.

attrs.title: Popcorn vs bobble
attrs.body: Bobble: five incomplete trebles, all loops closed at once. Softer, lower relief. Good for smaller yarn weights. Popcorn: five complete trebles, cluster lifted via the first treble top. Taller, more defined, firmer. Better for chunkier yarns and blanket squares where the texture needs to read from a distance.

attrs.heading: Popcorn problems
attrs.intro: Three problems specific to the popcorn.

items.symptom: The loop falls off while the hook is removed
items.cause: The working loop is too loose and drops off the hook during the re-insertion step.
items.fix: Drop the hook from the loop slowly and pinch the loop between thumb and forefinger before re-inserting into the first treble top. Alternatively, use a safety pin to hold the loop.

items.symptom: The popcorn top is untidy with a visible extra loop
items.cause: The hook re-inserted into the wrong position — into the chain between two trebles rather than into the first treble top.
items.fix: Identify the clear V of the very first treble before removing the hook. Mark it with a stitch marker on the first few popcorns until the position is familiar.

items.symptom: The popcorn sits flat against the fabric instead of popping up
items.cause: The five trebles were worked into different stitches instead of all into the same stitch, or the closing pull-through was too loose.
items.fix: All five trebles go into the same single stitch. The closing pull-through should be snug.

content.text: The puff stitch is the softer, rounded cousin of both the bobble and the popcorn. Where those use trebles, the puff uses extended half trebles (more loops, pulled tall). Try all three in the same swatch to understand where each belongs in a pattern.
